name: Enterprise Knowledge Landscape and Decision Dependency View
constraints: Knowledge Landscape is a governed non-catalogue profile declaration and Decision Dependency View is a reproducible non-catalogue projection; neither receives subject, catalogue or runtime identity.

The landscape handle and view fingerprint are administrative coordinates only; they cannot own assertions, act as a concept scheme, serve as an assertion store, decide validity, merge identities or mint identifiers in any source model.

Concepts and designations, scheme releases, claims, citation acts, governed documents and records, decision content and issued decision records retain the class-to-base mastership declared in mastershipMapping; non-governed Source Work remains unassigned and views never write back.

Every derived edge is a read-only reference whose registered edge type names its owning model and pins claim version, governed-record version or citation consulted-representation locator plus digest, scheme release, concept/designation version and decision release; unregistered or ownerless edge types are invalid.
A reproducible view fingerprint contains exact query rules, pinned source releases, evaluation timestamp and declared projection-loss classes; later observations never rewrite an earlier content pin.

Pins bind historical content only; access is always intersected at generation time against current source policy and landscape retrieval policy. Absent or unresolved access scope is most-restrictive and suppresses the derived result.

An auditable landscape declaration or view execution is persisted as a WM-REC-001 governed record with custody and versioning; WM-REC-010 is reserved for a declaration genuinely issued as a decision by competent authority and never turns a view into a decision subject.

Retraction and rebuttal append dated observations on their source masters and trigger notify-and-recheck traversal; for non-governed source work, status observations are carried on the WM-KNW-008 citation act against its consulted representation locator plus digest.

Each notify-and-recheck is a dated open dependency finding on WM-KNW-010, closes only through an explicit dated competent-authority act including explicit no-change, and never automatically changes decision status, deletes citation or rewrites rationale.
Notifications obey the same current-policy access intersection as all outputs; where no channel is authorized for both endpoints, only a non-leaking escalation marker is emitted.

A decision becomes reopened, superseded, revoked or remains-effective only through an explicit dated act whose authority attestation resolves on the issued WM-REC-010 record; unresolvable or non-competent acts are invalid.

Term identity is scheme-qualified, concept/designation-version pinned and release-bounded; shared labels, similarity, semantic relations, paraphrases or inclusion of multiple schemes never authorize concept merge or namespace unification.
Cross-scheme terminology conflicts are dated WM-KNW-018 observations that create no identity operation or new concept; dependency findings remain owned by the dependent decision in WM-KNW-010.

A claim without a citation remains unevidenced; absence of evidence is uncertainty rather than falsity or permission to invent a source. Citation to identifier-unassigned source work is a distinct state, neither unevidenced nor governed-record-evidenced.
Unknown, unevidenced, cited-to-unassigned-source, unsupported, refuted, missing binding, unresolved locator and dangling rationale remain distinct states in every projection.

Before generation, current source restrictions across every participating node are intersected with landscape retrieval policy and the most restrictive result governs indexes, closures, counts, co-citation, notifications, search results and summaries.

Restricted existence or correspondence cannot leak through identifiers, paraphrase, inference, path closure, cardinality differences, aggregates, repeated-query differencing or wording that reveals a shared source; suppression markers are emitted identically whether or not a protected item exists.

Redaction creates a new rendition with its own digest and preserved provenance and never overwrites the source; replay after restriction or redaction applies current policy and cannot redisclose historically pinned content.
Third-party, personal, licensed and records-management restrictions survive indexing and aggregation; disposed identifiers remain resolvable and are never reused.
holds: Evidence Artifact / Source Work remains identifier-unassigned; non-governed source observations use citation-act custody until that boundary resolves.
All bases remain non-canonical and several rely on single-provider waivers.
Required relation-ledger edges, semantic crosswalks, access-scope, citation deduplication, relation-direction and timestamp-offset semantics require reconciliation.
Canonical publication is held until the base, crosswalk, authority and rights contracts are ratified.
